elevator_pitch: An ultra-compact breakout for the Bosch BME280 — measuring barometric pressure (±1 hPa), relative humidity (±3 % RH), and temperature (±1 °C) — with selectable SPI or I²C interface and onboard regulation.
description:
The BME280 packs pressure, humidity, and temperature sensing into a tiny 2.5 mm × 2.5 mm LGA package, making board layout the primary challenge. This breakout routes the BME280's six-pad footprint with an exposed thermal pad to a 0.1-inch header and Qwiic I²C connector, while an SDO address selection solder bridge allows two BME280s on the same I²C bus.

SPI/I²C mode is selected by a three-position header: tie CSB to VCC for I²C; drive it low for SPI. Both modes are tested and documented in the accompanying Arduino library example. The onboard MIC5219 LDO regulates 3.3 V from a 3.3–6 V input, with a 10 µF input cap and 1 µF MLCC output cap for stability.

All passives are 0402 for compact layout. The PCB is 18 mm × 22 mm — small enough to fit inside an enclosure finger recess. Silkscreen markings include pin names, interface mode labels, and the Bosch part number for quick identification in a component bin.
